bib.title: Prismer: A Vision-Language Model with Multi-Task Experts

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Prismer: A Vision-Language Model with Multi-Task Experts. Shikun Liu, Linxi Fan, Edward Johns, Zhiding Yu, Chaowei Xiao, Anima Anandkumar (Imperial/NVIDIA/UW-Madison/Caltech). arXiv 2303.02506 v3 (18 Jan 2024). Preprint-style (no venue printed), first posted 2023.
COVERAGE: All 29 pages read (about 80,000 chars extracted, fully read, incl. conclusions/limitations, ablations, Appendix A hyperparameters, Appendix B training cost). References skimmed. Figure images not viewed (text from figure panels only; Fig 5 and Fig 4 values come from extracted axis labels). The extractor emitted fontTools warnings and embedded latexit blobs; both are harmless.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Prismer matches or beats similarly sized VLMs and approaches ones trained on 10-60x more data, using 12.7M image/text pairs. Only about 20% of parameters are trained; the vision and language backbones and the task experts are frozen.
  number: 12.7M pairs; BASE COCO CIDEr 135.1, NoCaps overall 109.1, VQAv2 test-dev 76.8; LARGE COCO CIDEr 136.5, NoCaps 112.9, VQAv2 78.4
  setup: Fine-tuned, 224px pre-train then 480px fine-tune. COCO Karpathy split, NoCaps val, VQAv2 (+Visual Genome). Table 3. Compared against BLIP at 129M pairs, LEMON at 200M, GIT at 0.8B.
  quote: "Both Prismer BASE and PrismerLARGE achieve comparable image captioning performance to BLIP [45] and LEMON [33], despite being trained on 10 and 20 times less data, respectively. Additionally, the PrismerLARGE model has achieved VQAv2 accuracy comparable to GIT [88], despite being trained on 60 times less data."
  where: p.11 (Table 3, p.11)
- claim: The frozen backbones account for most of the quality. The task experts add a smaller boost.
  number: +6 CIDEr (NoCaps out-of-domain, BASE); +1 VQAv2 accuracy (LARGE)
  setup: Prismer vs PrismerZ (no task experts). Table 3: NoCaps Out 111.7 vs 105.8 (BASE); VQAv2 test-dev 78.4 vs 77.5 (LARGE).
  quote: "which suggests that the strong backbone experts are primarily responsible for good generalisation. However, the task experts provide an additional boost in performance, particularly in image captioning tasks (such as a 6 CIDEr score increase in the NoCaps out-of-domain set in the BASE model) and in the LARGE model variant (such as a 1 VQAv2 accuracy increase in the LARGE model)."
  where: p.11
- claim: Zero-shot captioning is strong for the data used. Prismer LARGE gets 107.9 CIDEr on NoCaps zero-shot, against SimVLM HUGE at 101.4, with 140x less data. It also beats BLIP-2 at 107.5 (listed in the table).
  number: COCO zero-shot CIDEr 122.6 (BASE) and 129.7 (LARGE); NoCaps CIDEr 87.5 (BASE) and 107.9 (LARGE)
  setup: Fig 4 left. No fine-tuning. The caption states "state-of-the-art" for zero-shot.
  quote: "Prismer achieves state-of-the-art performance on the NoCaps dataset compared to SimVLM [90] by a large margin, whilst using 140 times less training data."
  where: p.11-12 (Fig 4 left)
- claim: Training cost is small. Prismer LARGE needs 8 days on 32 V100 GPUs. Its cost is 1.9 PFlops-days against 22.2 for BLIP LARGE and 66.9 for SimVLM. The expert models are excluded from this cost.
  number: 8 days on 32 V100; Table 8: Prismer BASE 0.66, LARGE 1.9 PFlops-days; inference 0.20 / 0.38 TFlops
  setup: Costs cover only building Prismer. "excluding all original pre-training data implied in the original expert models". Inference is estimated with 256 image tokens and 30 text tokens. Other models' costs are partly the authors' estimates.
  quote: "The largest model variant, Prismer LARGE, only requires 8 days of training on 32 NVIDIA V100 GPUs. This is significantly more efficient than previous state-of-the-art VLMs such as SimVLM [90] which requires 5 days of training on 2048 TPUv3, GIT-2 [88] which requires 1.5 months of training on 1500 NVIDIA A100s, and Flamingo [3] which requires 2 weeks of training on 1536 TPUv4."
  where: Appendix B, p.29
- claim: Parameter counts. PrismerBASE has 160M trainable of 980M total. PrismerLARGE has 360M trainable of 1.6B total. The totals include 654M parameters of the six task experts, needed at inference.
  number: 160M/980M; 360M/1.6B; PrismerZ BASE 105M/275M; PrismerZ LARGE 270M/870M; 654M experts; resampler about 50M
  setup: Table 2
  quote: "We count the total parameters required for data inference, which include the additional 6 task experts with a combined parameter size of 654M parameters in our Prismer model."
  where: p.9 (Table 2)
- claim: More experts help up to a plateau, better-quality experts help, and the model tolerates noise experts. Gains are small, under 1 point.
  number: Fig 5 VQAv2 acc: RGB only 72.17; +2 experts 72.64; +4 72.79; +6 72.82. Depth with 25% noise 72.44, 10% noise 72.52, clean 72.59. RGB+Noise 72.26, +Depth 72.59, +Depth & Noise 72.58.
  setup: BASE model, 3M pre-training data (CC+SBU), 224x224, VQAv2 test-dev. Single runs; differences are a few tenths of a point.
  quote: "Prismer maintains performance even when including experts that predict noise, as shown in Fig. 5c. Interestingly, adding noise can even result in a non-trivial improvement compared to training on RGB images alone, which can be considered as a form of implicit regularisation."
  where: p.14 (Fig 5)
- claim: Individual experts help the tasks you would expect. Object detection helps spatial and text VQA. Depth helps spatial reasoning. OCR helps text VQA. The effect is large on domain tasks, much larger than on general benchmarks.
  number: VSR zero-shot 65.6 (no experts) vs 68.7 (+6 experts); Text-VQA zero-shot 22.6 vs 28.8. Flamingo gets 35.0 on Text-VQA; BLIP-2 gets 15.7; OFA gets 18.3. Per-expert VSR: Depth 68.4, Normal 68.3, Edge 67.8, Seg 68.4, OCR 67.2, ObjDet 68.3. Text-VQA: Depth 27.4, OCR 28.4, ObjDet 28.4.
  setup: PrismerLARGE trained on VQAv2, evaluated zero-shot with one expert at a time. VSR zero-shot split; Text-VQA validation. Table 5. Per-expert gaps are small, so the cited "key experts" are read mostly from the green/red colour coding, which does not survive text extraction.
  quote: "the substantial performance improvement observed (compared to general reasoning tasks presented in Table 3) when comparing Prismer to PrismerZ (with no experts) underscores the pivotal role played by the experts in domain-specific reasoning tasks."
  where: p.15-16 (Table 5)
- claim: Freezing the backbones is essential. Unfreezing hurts accuracy and raises step time.
  number: VQAv2 72.79 default; freeze vision only 70.49; freeze language only 67.77; all params 68.13 (step time 1.15x). Fine-tuning: freeze vision+lang 71.36; freeze lang only 70.37; all 68.69.
  setup: Table 6, BASE, reduced training, 3 experts (depth, normal, segmentation)
  quote: "freezing pre-trained parameters is essential for achieving strong performance and avoiding over-fitting and catastrophic forgetting of the learned knowledge."
  where: p.16-17 (Table 6 vi-vii)
- claim: Resampler ablation. Too many latents or a heavy design hurts. Default is 4 layers, 64 latents. A resampler that sees RGB too (Full Perceiver) drops to 65.05. 128 latents gives 70.28, 256 gives 68.07. Random sampling instead of a learned resampler gives 72.24.
  number: see list
  setup: Table 6 (iii)-(v), VQAv2 test-dev. Adaptor: bottleneck 1/2 gives 72.52, 1/4 gives 71.66; a gated residual MLP gives 70.54.
  quote: "using lightweight designs for the resampler layers and latent variables is crucial for stable training."
  where: p.16 (text), p.17 (Table 6)
- claim: Design. The vision encoder is a frozen CLIP ViT (B/16 or L/14). The decoder is a frozen RoBERTa (BASE/LARGE). Six experts feed it: depth (DPT), surface normal (NLL-AngMF), edge (DexiNed), segmentation (Mask2Former), object detection (UniDet) and OCR (CharNet). Only the Experts Resampler, the per-task convolution stems and the Adaptors are trained. A single next-token loss is used. OPT and BLOOM decoders did worse in early tests.
  number: 6 experts; 5 conv layers of 3x3 per stem; CLIP text embedding PCA-reduced to 64 channels; instance embedding size 128; semantic label resolution down-sampled 4x
  setup: Sec 3, Table 1
  quote: "the Experts Resampler learns a pre-defined number of latent input queries, to cross-attend a flattened embedding concatenated from all multi-task features."
  where: p.6-9
- claim: Experts differ from MoE. The experts are independently pre-trained black-box models whose explicit outputs are fed as input. This is unlike mixture-of-experts, where experts are sub-modules of one network.
  quote: "in Prismer, the 'experts' are independently pre-trained models, encodingexplicit knowledge based on their pre-trained tasks or domains."
  where: p.4
- claim: Contrast with LLM-as-controller pipelines (Socratic models, ViperGPT, Visual Programming). Those are zero-shot, errors in earlier experts propagate, and they are limited to the experts' domains. Prismer trains an integrated architecture that is more robust to non-optimal experts.
  quote: "errors predicted by previous experts can be carried forward to future experts."
  where: p.4

LIMITS
- No in-context or few-shot prompting by design, because the language model is small.
- Limited adaptability to a different expert, such as a segmentation model trained on another dataset. A notable performance drop.
- Features from all experts are entangled during pre-training, so using only some experts at inference drops performance notably. A masked-autoencoding objective did not fix this and degraded fine-tuned results.
- Generative only; less suited to discriminative tasks (retrieval, visual entailment).
- Still a clear gap to CoCa, GIT-2 and PaLI (e.g. VQAv2 78.4 vs 81.7 for GIT-2 and 84.3 for PaLI). The authors say those need far more cost and private data.
- Few-shot ImageNet performance is below GIT and Flamingo.
- Expert labels are converted to image-like tensors; the authors suggest text-token representations might be better.
- Inference needs all six expert models, plus preprocessing of labels.
- Ablations use a reduced setup: 3M data, 224px, BASE. Fig 5 gains are tenths of a point, and no variance across seeds is given.
- Dated: 2023, small CLIP + RoBERTa backbones. Later VLMs and LLM-based models are not covered.

BUILDS ON: Flamingo (Alayrac 2022, Perceiver-style resampler, concatenated K/V); Perceiver (Jaegle 2021); CLIP (Radford 2021, cited as [68]); RoBERTa; ViT (Dosovitskiy 2020); adapters (Houlsby 2019); BLIP (Li 2022, captioner used to re-caption web data); GIT/SimVLM (single autoregressive objective); Socratic Models (Zeng 2022), ViperGPT, Visual Programming (Gupta & Kembhavi 2023); Taskonomy (Zamir 2018) for the multi-task choice; MultiMAE (Bachmann 2022); Ghiasi 2021 (multi-task self-training); Xiao 2021 (early convolutions); LiT (Zhai 2022) for freezing.

CODE: none (repo at github.com/NVlabs/prismer). Hyperparameters (Appendix A, Table 7): AdamW, wd 0.05, cosine schedule, pre-train LR 3e-4 (BASE) / 1e-4 (LARGE) with 2000 warm-up steps, batch 1024, 20 epochs, 224px. Fine-tune LR 5e-5 at 480px (COCO/NoCaps: 3 epochs, batch 256; VQAv2: 10 epochs, batch 512) and 384px (ImageNet: 20 epochs, batch 64). Evaluation: beam size 3 with the prefix "A picture of"; VQA and classification are scored by ranking log-likelihoods over a fixed answer list.

FIGURES (not rendered; captions from text)
- Fig 1 (p.2): Prismer overview. One image yields segmentation, depth, detection, normal, edge and OCR labels, then captioning and VQA. Good as the opening diagram.
- Fig 2 (p.5): Architecture. RGB and expert patchify feed an Experts Resampler into a bi-directional vision encoder with Adaptors, then cross-attention into a causal language decoder. Frozen versus trainable parts are marked.
- Fig 3 (p.8): Experts Resampler (variable-length input, fixed latent count) and Adaptor (down-project, squared ReLU, up-project, residual).
- Fig 4 (p.12): Zero-shot captioning table and few-shot ImageNet curves.
- Fig 5 (p.15): VQAv2 versus number, quality and noise of experts.
- Table 1 (p.7): expert, dataset, model and parameters. Table 3: the benchmark comparison. Table 6: the ablations.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 5 loses its green/red colour coding in extraction, so which experts count as "most helpful" is unverified beyond the numbers. The Fig 5 and Fig 4 values were taken from extracted axis text and are consistent with the prose. Reference [1] is malformed in the source. Table 6 rows have partial layout loss; the changed-setting values were read in order.
